name: install-main
description: Set up a local MemQL cluster built from the latest source on this machine, instead of from a published release.

steps.label: Checking this computer
steps.description: Taking stock of this machine before anything is installed: what system it is, which supporting tools are already here, whether Docker is answering, whether the ports a cluster needs are free, and how much disk is left. Only a system MemQL cannot support stops the install here; the rest is reported for you to read.

steps.label: Checking Docker
steps.description: Checking that Docker can run containers for you, before anything is installed.

steps.label: Installing tools
steps.description: Installing k3d, which runs the cluster, and checking the download is the expected one.

steps.label: Installing tools
steps.description: Installing kubectl, which talks to the cluster, and checking the download is the expected one.

steps.label: Installing tools
steps.description: Installing mkcert, which issues this machine's local certificates, and checking the download is the expected one.

steps.label: Adding local addresses
steps.description: Pointing the cluster's web addresses at this machine, inside a marked section of the system hosts file.

steps.label: Setting up browser trust
steps.description: Setting up the tools your browsers need to trust this machine's local certificates.
steps.retainedReason: certutil is a general system tool other software uses. MemQL installs it because without it Firefox and Chrome cannot trust the local CA and the front door is unreachable in a browser -- but an application uninstaller that removes distribution packages is how installers earn their reputation, so this one is never taken back.

steps.label: Creating certificates
steps.description: Issuing the certificate that lets this cluster answer over https.

steps.label: Downloading MemQL
steps.description: Downloading the MemQL release you chose.

steps.label: Checking AI access
steps.description: Checking that this cluster's AI provider credential is accepted, before the cluster is built around it. Skipped when no federation ids were supplied: installing spends no AI credit, and providers are set up afterwards in MemQL OS.

steps.label: Creating the cluster
steps.description: Creating the cluster and preparing it for the MemQL images that are about to be built here.

steps.label: Building MemQL
steps.description: Building MemQL from the source just downloaded and starting the cluster on it.

steps.label: Creating your account
steps.description: Creating your owner account and applying the settings you gave, then restarting the services that read them.

steps.label: Checking secure access
steps.description: Checking the cluster answers over https at every one of its addresses.

steps.label: Preparing sign-in
steps.description: Looking for a sign-in link for the owner account, as a second way in. A cluster that has not been asked for one carries none, which is reported rather than treated as a failure.

steps.label: Preparing sign-in
steps.description: Creating a single-use link for setting up a passkey on the owner account. This install names that owner as the cluster starts, so the link is normally ready here; a cluster started without owner details has nobody to enrol yet, and that is reported instead.

steps.label: Creating your recovery key
steps.description: Claiming this cluster's recovery key and showing it once, so you finish with a way back in if every other is ever lost. The key is minted for the owner as the cluster starts, so a first install normally ends holding one; a cluster started without owner details has nobody to mint one for, and a key an earlier run already claimed is left alone, because only its fingerprint was kept and re-showing it is impossible.
